session_summary: Pre-deploy stress test of Voltron Glimpse. project-planner authored docs/stress-test-plan.md (11-vector methodology). qa-tester built a fake-driven harness under scripts/stress/ (no new runtime deps, temp-root-only writes, 127.0.0.1-only) and ran smoke (5/5 PASS) + abbreviated soak (6/6 PASS); npm test 132/132 green; V1 maxBuffer ceiling measured at ~6766 docker-ps rows. committer made c88453d (23 files), pushed to origin. bd stats: 67 total, 64 closed, 3 open (glimpse-mwm V11 host-smoke escalated to user; glimpse-1mm + glimpse-58g hardening findings filed as backlog).

agent_feedback.worked_well: Source-grounded the harness against real injection seams (pollDocker exec, createDockerLogTailer spawn, createReconciler timer); correctly classified ceilings vs findings and never edited app code under test.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: The first qa-tester dispatch (build entire harness + run smoke in one go) hit the 10-minute container wall-clock cap mid-run. The agent has no awareness of the wall-clock budget vs the max_turns budget, so it front-loaded all file writing and ran out of time before the validation run.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Add guidance to qa-tester (and the scrum-master sizing table) that container dispatches have a ~10-min wall-clock cap independent of max_turns; for build+run tasks, write files early and incrementally so a timeout leaves a runnable artifact, and prefer splitting 'build harness' from 'run+validate' into separate dispatches.

overall_notes: Key orchestration lesson: the ~10-min container wall-clock cap is the real sizing constraint, not max_turns. The first build+run dispatch timed out, but because the workspace is mounted, all 13 harness files persisted — a focused re-dispatch (run+fix+report only) then completed in <2 min. Sizing future build+run tasks as two dispatches (build, then run/validate) avoids the wasted timeout. Tools used: alexandria not needed (no new tool setup this session).
